ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a table comparing stain-removing effects, with the column headings in order being “enzyme-added laundry detergent A”, “enzyme-added laundry detergent B”, “enzyme-added laundry detergent C”, and “enzyme-free laundry detergent (control)”, and the row items are “blood stain” and “oil stain”. The table shows: for blood stains, enzyme-added laundry detergent A is “+++”, enzyme-added laundry detergent B is “+”, enzyme-added laundry detergent C is “+++”, and enzyme-free laundry detergent is “+”; for oil stains, enzyme-added laundry detergent A is “+”, enzyme-added laundry detergent B is “+++”, enzyme-added laundry detergent C is “+++”, and enzyme-free laundry detergent is “+”. Then reason: The question stem states that the more “+”, the better the stain-removing effect. The stain-removing effect of enzyme-added laundry detergent A on blood stains is clearly stronger than that of the enzyme-free control, while its effect on oil stains is the same as that of the enzyme-free control, indicating that A mainly enhances the ability to remove blood stains. Blood stains mainly contain protein, and the enzyme that can decompose protein stains is protease. Therefore, the enzyme added to enzyme-added laundry detergent A is protease.
